parts:
Just spotted an interesting discussion on the Cython mailing list. It
looks like there's a MinGW toolchain that might make supporting
PyStan on Windows easier.

----- Forwarded message from Sturla Molden <sturla...@gmail.com> -----

> From: Sturla Molden <sturla...@gmail.com>
> To: cython...@googlegroups.com
> Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2015 18:23:54 +0000 (UTC)
> Subject: [cython-users] Re: C++11 & Cython & windows & python 2.7
>
> Ian Bell <ian.h...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> > So if I understand correctly, if you use the stock python (from conda,
> > python.org, etc.) it should still be possible to use MINGW+C++11?
>
> Yes, definately. You can use MinGW for C++11 with the stock Python.
>
> I will recommend the MinGW-w64 static toolchain made for NumPy and SciPy by
> Carl Kleffner, not the vanilla MinGW. There are certain reasons for this,
> such as linking the C++ standard lib to the correct CRT and using the
> correct stack alignment in 32 bit binaries (MSVC and MinGW differ by
> default). It is all taken care if in this toolchain. Note that it is to
> some extent a bloatware generator because it will statically link all
> runtime libraries except the CRT.
>
>
> > Another question in the same vein - anyone have any success compiling
> > python and python extensions using Intel compiler?
>
> Yes on Mac.
>
> I do not know if icc allows us to control the C run-time DLL with which to
> link on Windows. Ask Intel.
>
> icpc generally gives faster code than g++ or clang++, but the difference is
> not very large.
>
>
> Sturla
>
>
> > On Thu, Jul 2, 2015 at 11:46 AM, Sturla Molden <sturla...@gmail.com>
> > wrote:
> >
> >> Ian Bell <ian.h...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >>
> >>> As I understand it, MINGW compilation would be my only option
> >>> in windows for python 2.7, as there is no way to use C++11 in VS2008 (for
> >>> python 2.7) or VS2010 (for python 3.4).
> >>>
> >>> Anyone have experience with this? Is this a MINGW-only solution on
> >>> windows?
> >>
> >> You need to recompile Python (and all the exensions you need) in order to
> >> use a different MSVC compiler than the one used to build the official
> >> binaries from python.org. MinGW is easier because it allows you to select
> >> the C runtime with which to link.
> >>
> >> Sturla
